deals.headline: Grupo Carso sells 51% of Real Oviedo to Grupo Pachuca
deals.source_name: Real Oviedo (official statement of Grupo Carso)
deals.summary: Carlos Slim's Grupo Carso, majority owner since 2012, accepted Grupo Pachuca's offer: Pachuca to hold 51%, Carso 20% and thousands of small shareholders 29%. No price was disclosed (Palco23 notes Carso had bought in for close to EUR 2m in 2012; 2Playbook says Carso invested over EUR 23m in total).

deals.investor: Grupo Pachuca (almost all; minority shareholders about EUR 60,000)
deals.summary: Capital increase of EUR 2.36m taking share capital to EUR 24.3m, used to absorb past losses and lift the squad-cost limit; Grupo Pachuca covered practically all of it.

deals.evidence: por 2,8 millones de euros desembolsados por el máximo accionista del club, Promotora de Inversión del Deporte
deals.headline: EUR 2.8m capital increase paid by the largest shareholder
deals.investor: Promotora de Inversión del Deporte, S.A. de C.V. (the club's largest shareholder)
deals.summary: Launched as a EUR 3.7m increase (344,112 new shares at EUR 10.75, per 2Playbook) to lift the squad-cost limit; Palco23 reports that EUR 2.8m was paid in on 2 August 2023 by the club's largest shareholder, Promotora de Inversión del Deporte. The club's accounts show EUR 2,863,134 of capital increases in 2023/24.

deals.headline: Real Oviedo has drawn EUR 7.8m of LaLiga Impulso (CVC) participating loans

name: Real Oviedo, S.A.D.
notes: Promoted to La Liga in 2025, relegated again at the end of 2025-26: the club plays 2026-27 in LaLiga Hypermotion (LaLiga's own club page lists it there); the league field is left as given. The latest accounts (2024/25, Segunda División season, FY to 30 June 2025) are a scanned PDF with no text layer, so revenue and the broadcast line are taken from Palco23's report of them (exact importe neto de la cifra de negocios in the accounts: EUR 23,098,971, 2023/24: EUR 20,024,610; broadcasting EUR 7,238,523), while operating and pre-tax results, the CVC drawdown and both shareholder stakes carry the figures as printed in the scanned PDF and may fail an automated text check. The net loss of EUR 5,578,650 is also stated in text by La Nueva España. Other 2024/25 lines: season tickets/members EUR 5,068,747; competitions EUR 1,972,266; merchandising EUR 3,039,208; advertising EUR 5,780,227; sporting squad costs EUR 16,599,553 and non-sporting staff EUR 3,006,709 (no single wage total is printed, so wages is null; La Nueva España's breakdown mislabels some of these lines). Negative equity of EUR 3.3m at 30 June 2025. Whether Promotora de Inversión del Deporte is Grupo Pachuca's vehicle is not stated in the accounts, and neither is whether Soinmob/Control Empresarial de Capitales is the former Grupo Carso stake. Both are likely, but no page read says so. No valuation, attendance average or social follower total found on a citable page. The CEO/president role is shown in the June 2026 organigram without names. In January 2025 the club cut its share capital by EUR 12m to absorb accumulated losses (capital now EUR 15,164,298 in 2,527,383 shares of EUR 6).

ownership_summary: Real Oviedo SAD has been controlled since 2022 by Mexico's Grupo Pachuca (Jesús Martínez Patiño). In July 2022 it agreed to buy 51% from Carlos Slim's Grupo Carso, with Carso keeping 20% and thousands of small shareholders 29%; it then led capital increases in 2023. The 2024/25 audited accounts list two shareholders above 10% at 30 June 2025: Promotora de Inversión del Deporte, S.A. de C.V. with 59.97% (Palco23 calls it the club's largest shareholder and says it paid the August 2023 capital increase), and Soinmob Inmobiliaria Española, S.A.U. with 15.45%, a subsidiary of Control Empresarial de Capitales, S.A. de C.V. Carso first entered in a November 2012 capital increase; the club says it has around 50,000 shareholders in more than 125 countries. In February 2026 president Martín Peláez said Grupo Pachuca would not sell.
